name: Everline Property Group

faqs.q: What types of property do you handle?
faqs.a: Residential resale, new construction, condominiums, revenue duplexes and small multi-family, plus acreages inside the Regina commuter belt. We do not list commercial or agricultural land, and we will refer you to a specialist rather than learn on your file.

faqs.q: How do I know if a property is a good investment?
faqs.a: We run the numbers before you write an offer: purchase price, realistic Regina rent for the unit type, condo or maintenance reserve, property tax from the SAMA assessment, vacancy allowance, and financing at your actual approved rate. If the cash flow does not clear, we say so.

faqs.q: Do I need to hire a real estate agent to buy?
faqs.a: No, but in Saskatchewan the seller's commission agreement almost always covers the buyer's agent, so representation typically costs a buyer nothing directly. What you get is someone whose duty of care is to you and not to the listing.

faqs.q: What is the process for buying a property?
faqs.a: Financing pre-approval, a written needs list, showings, offer with conditions, inspection and financing condition period, condition removal, lawyer and title transfer, then possession. Most Regina purchases run 30 to 60 days from accepted offer to keys.

faqs.q: Can I tour a property before purchasing?
faqs.a: Yes. Every active listing on this site can be booked directly from its page, and we will hold a video walkthrough if you are out of province. Second showings before an offer are normal and we encourage them.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to sell my home with Everline?
faqs.a: A published commission schedule, given to you in writing before you sign anything, including exactly what the co-operating brokerage receives. Professional photography, floor plans, staging consultation and the marketing budget are included, not billed back.

faqs.q: How accurate is the online home valuation?
faqs.a: The instant estimate is a starting range built from recent comparable sales in your neighbourhood. It cannot see your renovations, your lot, or your condition. Treat it as a bracket, then have us walk the property for a real number.

neighbourhoods.name: Harbour Landing
neighbourhoods.blurb: Regina's largest modern build-out. Wide streets, new schools, and the shortest walk to groceries in the city's south end.

neighbourhoods.name: Cathedral
neighbourhoods.blurb: Character homes, mature elms, and the densest stretch of independent cafés and restaurants in Saskatchewan.

neighbourhoods.name: Lakeview
neighbourhoods.blurb: Backing onto Wascana Park. Mid-century bungalows on generous lots, tightly held and rarely on the market long.

neighbourhoods.name: The Greens on Gardiner
neighbourhoods.blurb: East-end executive homes wrapped around green space, with quick access to the Ring Road and the airport run.

neighbourhoods.name: White City
neighbourhoods.blurb: Fifteen minutes east on Highway 1. Acreage-sized lots, no city tax, and the best value per square foot in the region.

neighbourhoods.name: Downtown & Warehouse District
neighbourhoods.blurb: Converted warehouse lofts and concrete towers. The strongest rental yields in the city for a one-bedroom hold.
